findings.title: Raw recovery codes are serialized and passed to the user storage provider in plaintext
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() serializes the full list of freshly generated recovery codes as JSON and passes them as the challenge response of a UserCredentialModel to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). Unlike the local credential provider, which stores only salted/hashed codes (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel hashes each code), this hands the clear-text codes to arbitrary third-party UserStorageProviders, which will typically persist them as-is (the testsuite provider in this PR does exactly that, see BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential). This turns a hashed-at-rest credential into a plaintext secret store and may also log/expose codes through provider implementations. At minimum the codes should be hashed before being handed out, or the contract documented explicitly.

findings.title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never marked as used, so a single code can be replayed indefinitely
findings.body: After a successful validation the authenticator obtains the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(), which may now return a credential built on the fly from the federated/user-storage provider (see BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials, which reconstructs the model from all codes each call). Because the authenticator only reads the model and never writes back the updated "used codes" state for the federated case (and cannot, since there is no update path), every code remains valid forever and allCodesUsed() never becomes true, so CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES is never re-triggered. Recovery codes are intended to be single-use; this allows unlimited replay of one captured code.

findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get() can throw NoSuchElementException rendering the login form
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) returns an Optional, and credentialModelOpt.get() is called without checking isPresent(). If neither the user storage nor local storage holds a recovery-codes credential (e.g. the provider returned nothing or deserialization failed, in which case BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials silently drops the credential), the login page rendering fails with an unhandled NoSuchElementException / 500 instead of a proper error.

findings.title: getCredentials() NPEs for users not present in the in-memory map
findings.body: getCredentials() calls getMyUser(user) and immediately dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check, while every other method in this class (isConfiguredFor, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, isValid) explicitly guards against a null MyUser. For any UserModel whose username is not in the map (e.g. stale cache entry or local user mapped to this provider) this throws a NullPointerException during credential enumeration, breaking login/account pages rather than returning an empty stream.

findings.title: Test user storage never consumes a used recovery code
findings.body: isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE returns true whenever the submitted code matches any stored code, and never removes/marks it used. The provider therefore accepts the same code an unlimited number of times, which does not model single-use recovery codes and means the new test testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin cannot detect the missing code-consumption behaviour in the production path.

findings.title: Recovery-codes credential cannot be disabled/removed from the test user storage
findings.body: supportsCredentialType and isConfiguredFor were extended for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE, but disableCredentialType() and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() still handle only OTP. As a consequence an admin/account action to delete the recovery-codes credential stored in this provider is silently ignored (disableCredentialType logs "Unsupported"), and the test suite has no coverage for removing user-storage recovery codes.

findings.title: getCredentials builds credential model from raw codes, double-hashing and discarding the stored id
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues() hashes the values it is given, but here it is fed the plaintext codes stored in credentialData and the resulting model keeps no id (the generated recoveryCodes.getId() is not propagated). Code paths such as RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator, which call removeStoredCredentialById(model.getId()), therefore operate on a null id, and the hashes in the returned model are inconsistent with what isValid() compares against.
